artifact: §12 — every disagreement classified to a root cause

classes.A: evaluator defect — the evaluator violates the written contract
classes.B: contract ambiguity — the written contract does not adjudicate between the readings the reviewers applied
classes.C: reviewer inconsistency — a reviewer contradicts their own stated rule
classes.D: consensus-construction defect — the majority rule or denominator is wrong
classes.E_F_G: Phase-3 production defect — the IR is wrong, incomplete or mis-attributed
classes.H: source ambiguity — the source text itself admits more than one reading

creditEligibility.detail: all 3 non-unanimous credit cases (doc-a::I::applicable-ebitda, fwrg-6.04-a-iii, lsb-6.02-liens) turn on whether the ground-truth proposition itself is one claim or several — class H.

surfacingStatus.detail: all 14 turn on AMB-1: whether a claim-specific flag on one sub-part surfaces a composite claim. Adjudicator A applies INVARIANT_5 ('dominant material content'); B and C apply INVARIANT_3 ('any claim-specific flag'). All three cite the SAME facts.

workedExample.facts: Section 7.1 states four maintenance financial covenants. Only 7.1(d), the springing liquidity test, carries a claim-specific NEEDS_REVIEW flag. The two primary leverage covenants 7.1(a)/(b) carry none. All three adjudicators record exactly these facts.
workedExample.adjudicatorA: NOT_SPECIFICALLY_SURFACED — the flagged sub-part is not the dominant material content of the claim (INVARIANT_5)
workedExample.adjudication: the written contract adjudicates between INVARIANT_3 and INVARIANT_5 NOWHERE. This is not an evidence disagreement; it is an underspecified rule. Class B.

complianceNote: §3: a disagreement between evaluator and reviewer was not treated as proof of a production defect. Each was traced to the specific rule the parties applied and to whether the contract decides between them.
